issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Rideable.messageOnRide() as a no-argument method returning a String, and the template's example Main invokes messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) (and Pig/Seal implement this signature). This parameter mismatch changes the required method signature and return content, creating a structural conflict: students following the specification will implement a no-arg method that does not match the solution/tests, and the provided example usage in Main will not compile against the solution's interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface consistent with the problem statement and template Main: change Rideable.messageOnRide to a no-argument method (String messageOnRide()), and update Pig and Seal to implement the no-arg signature, returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, template Main (method calls and examples), and tests to reflect messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust the expected return text accordingly.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified in the problem (UML and instructions) and used in the template Main() as a no-argument method returning a String (messageOnRide():String). In the solution repository, Rideable.messageOnRide has a different signature (messageOnRide(String equipment)) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) require an equipment parameter. This mismatch changes the API students are expected to implement and breaks the direct mapping from the problem/template to the solution (and would cause compilation errors for code expecting the no-arg method).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide method consistent with the problem/template by removing the equipment parameter. Update Rideable to declare String messageOnRide(); and change Pig and Seal implementations to provide a no-argument messageOnRide() that returns the expected string (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle" / "Riding on Seal Clarabelle"). Alternatively, if equipment is intentional, update the problem statement and template Main usage to reflect the parameterized signature and its intended use.
